newsitem.title: IRAQ: Saddam says ties with U.N. could reach a deadlock.
newsitem.headline: Saddam says ties with U.N. could reach a deadlock.

text.p: President Saddam Hussein said on Thursday Iraq's ties with the United Nations could reach a deadlock if the Security Council did not take measures to lift trade sanctions soon.
In an address marking the July 17 revolution that brought his ruling Baath party to power 29 years ago, Saddam said Iraq had honoured its obligations and demanded the U.N. do something in return.

"As we do not want for the relations between Iraq and the Security Council...to reach a deadlock, we hope that the Council will take measures that could convince us that it has actually started to fulfil its obligations," Saddam said in a speech that was distributed by the Iraqi News Agency minutes after he began reading it on television.
Saddam blamed the recent standoff between Baghdad and the U.N. Special Commission (UNSCOM) in charge of dismantling Iraq's prohibited weapons on the United States.

"Because the people of Iraq support their leader and hold on to their rights of sovereignty, the American administration was urging the Security Council last June to adopt a draft resolution to ban Iraqi nationals from traveling abroad," he said.

Saddam said Turkey would not be able to ensure its security across its southern border without coordinating with Baghdad and ending the mandate of a Turkish-based U.S.-British force that patrols a no-fly zone in northern Iraq. The force is to protect Iraqi Kurds from possible attacks from Baghdad.
Saddam criticised Turkey's military pacts with Israel, saying such a rapprochement between them arose "apprehension and suspicion and may lead to hostility" with Arab states.
Commenting on the deadlocked Arab-Israeli peace process Saddam urged Arab countries that have ties with the Jewish state to freeze them and demanded Arabs the Palestinians.
